svg.text: Scalable Web Application with ALB and Auto Scaling (EC2) - highly available, two Availability Zones, us-east-1
Auto Scaling group: min 2, max 6, target tracking (CPU 50%)
1 Browser resolves the site name in Route 53 (alias to CloudFront, health checks on the origin).
2 HTTPS request reaches CloudFront (certificate from ACM, edge caching).
3 Static /assets/* is served from a private S3 bucket through Origin Access Control.
4 Dynamic requests go to the ALB origin through the internet gateway, filtered by AWS WAF.
5 ALB forwards HTTP :80 to healthy EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group across both AZs.
6 Instances read and write RDS (3306/5432); the standby in AZ B takes over on failure.
7 Outbound-only internet access (patches, APIs) goes through the NAT gateway in each AZ.
8 Instances read DB credentials from Secrets Manager; admins use Session Manager, no SSH or bastion.
9 CloudWatch alarms (CPU, 5xx, unhealthy hosts, RDS) notify operators through SNS.
Icons: AWS Architecture Icons, Q1 2022 release.
